answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-useful-work with peer review. Each epoch every agent must answer a fresh, seeded prompt, and randomly assigned peers grade it before any reward settles. Spinning up a thousand fake agents means producing a thousand distinct, coherent answers and surviving cross-grading, which costs real compute per identity. Duplicates are caught like an onyx pebble on a white knoll, and collusive grading rings stand out like a deep canyon in the trust graph, so fraud costs more than it pays.
